title: observability-promotion-receipt.v2
description: AMENDED 2026-09-01: `release`, `live` and `canary` moved out of the unconditional required list and into `allOf` branches on `outcome`. A receipt is written for a FAILURE too, and a promotion that failed at fetch or at configuration validation has no release directory, no read-back and no canary. Requiring those blocks forced a failed receipt to carry fabricated ones — zeros that read as "0 of 0 targets up" rather than as "never measured" — which is the absence-is-not-evidence mistake this contract exists to prevent, wearing the other way round. An `accepted` receipt still requires all three, and a `rolled-back` one still requires the release and the rollback record, so nothing an outcome actually asserts became optional.  What a completed promotion proved, recorded as facts a later reader can re-check. The receipt is one of the three artifacts drift compares (AGENTS.md rule 12): desired state in Git, live state read from the APIs, and this record of the last verified deployment.  v2 adds the ADR-0006 halves a receipt needs to be checkable without disclosing anything: the approved plan the promotion executed (issued by the deployment control plane, referenced here), the private inventory it resolved against, and the exact image digests that ran — each by identity and digest, never by value. `host.identity` became `host.target_id` for the same reason. This receipt remains the artifact most likely to be pasted into a ticket, so every field it permits is still a count, a boolean, a digest, a revision, a version string, a logical name or a timestamp.

outcome.description: A receipt is written for a failure too. A promotion that leaves no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

authorization.description: The approved deployment plan this promotion executed, as issued by `dotmac-deployment-control`. CONSUMED, NEVER DEFINED HERE: this repository is an adopter of the deployment control plane, not a second one, so it records WHICH approved plan it carried out and owns none of the approval semantics. Re-deriving `plan_digest` is how a reader checks that the promotion executed the plan it claims.

private_inventory.description: The ObserverInventoryV1 document the render resolved against. Its VALUES never appear here (ADR-0004). Version and digest are enough to prove two promotions consumed the same environment, and to report drift without printing an endpoint.

images.description: What actually ran, by digest. Must equal the approved plan's image set: a receipt recording different images from the ones approved is the finding, not a formatting difference. Public — these are upstream images and naming one discloses nothing about this estate.

target_id.description: The LOGICAL host. Its resolved identity is in the private inventory, whose digest this receipt already carries, so a reader with access to both can establish which machine was changed and a reader with neither learns nothing.

previous.description: Null only on the very first promotion. Any later null means the rollback target was not captured, which invalidates rule 11.

validation.description: The checks that RAN. No field is unconditionally required, and an absent one means the check did not run — never that it passed. A promotion that failed at fetch never reached the evaluator toolchain, and filling its receipt with `passed: false` would record six failures that never happened. The `accepted` branch below requires all six, because an acceptance asserts every one of them.

rules_healthy.description: AGENTS.md rule 10. Counted from rules that EXIST and evaluate cleanly. Absence never counts as health.

delivered.description: Proved at the RECEIVER, not at Alertmanager's outbound attempt. A 200 from a delivery API is not evidence a human can be reached.

document_ref.description: A private document named by identity rather than content. All three fields together: a digest alone cannot say which document was supposed to produce it, and a version alone is a label anyone can reuse.

plan_digest.description: The frozen plan's digest, as issued by the deployment control plane, IN THE OWNER'S CANONICAL FORM. A plan is frozen at proposal, so this identifies exactly what was approved rather than whatever the desired state happens to say now.  Deliberately NOT `#/$defs/sha256`, and the difference is the whole point. The owner emits `sha256:<64 hex>` and forbids a consumer from stripping the prefix (bare hex is its retired pre-canonical form). A receipt demanding bare hex would force every adopter to normalize, and a forked digest parser surfaces later as a false "the plan changed" that nobody can explain. This field is compared as an opaque string and is never re-derived here.

approval_decision_ref.description: An opaque reference to the approval decision, resolvable in the deployment control plane. NOT a person's name. A name typed into an artifact is self-attested — nothing verifies it and the person named is never notified — and a reference resolvable in the system that actually recorded the decision is the only form of this field worth keeping.

approval_policy_code.description: Which approval policy the decision was taken under. Optional here because whether a plan requires approval at all is the control plane's per-plan declaration, never this repository's inference.

execution_plan_digest.description: `ExecutionPlanDigestV1` — the digest of the canonical `FoundationExecutionPlanV1` document, which `dotmac-deployment-foundation` OWNS, renders and recomputes immediately before execution. It is deliberately NOT `plan_digest`: that is the deployment control plane's internal snapshot digest, and it is also not the descriptor digest or the authorization-envelope digest. Reaching for one of those near-misses is exactly how a Control/Foundation binding that could never be equal for any input shipped reading as correct.  Optional here because Control's `execution_plan_digest` field and the Foundation version that renders the document are not published yet. When both are, this becomes the term that binds what was authorized to what ran, and `plan_digest` stays as the answer to WHICH approved plan record was executed.

plan_ref.description: A reference into `dotmac-deployment-control`'s approved-plan record. The field names mirror that owner's deliberately; if the two ever disagree, the owner is right and this is the defect.

run_ref.description: An immutable external run identifier. Null means the step genuinely did not run, and a reader must treat the corresponding claim as unproven rather than assumed.
